title: Variant Safety Ladder — wireframe notes and backlog
content:
Purpose
---
Notes for a new UI metaphor: the 'Variant Safety Ladder'. This is a compact visual/editor for composing staged rollouts and fallback severity using a single horizontal control. Goal: give operators an at-a-glance sense of how brittle a route is, and an easy way to add automated fallbacks that escalate gracefully across model variants, regions, or capacity tiers.

High-level concept
---
- Ladder is a horizontally stacked set of lanes from left (strict) to right (lenient). Each rung maps to a fallback band: primary model -> smaller model variant -> quantized variant -> serve-from-cache -> region fallback -> degrade-to-embed-only.
- Each rung has a small electron (pill) representing behavior: rollout percent, probe thresholds (latency/error), auto-promote conditions, and circuit-breaker actions.
- The center of the control shows the current active rung and recent health (mini sparkline for latency and error rate).

Why this helps (product reasoning)
---
- Many teams think in severity levels (strict vs permissive) not in boolean fallbacks; ladder maps to that mental model.
- Consolidates multiple fallback policies (model variants, region, capacity tier) into one composable timeline.
- Enables single-click emergency rollback: slide to left-most rung to force strict (fail closed) or to far-right to allow degraded behavior.

Wireframe notes (annotations for designers/engineers)
---
1) Compact editor view (list/compact)
   - Left: route selector (model + route name).
   - Center: safety ladder control (SVG horizontal stack). Each rung clickable to expand details inline.
   - Right: action bar (preview, save, deploy-canary).
   - Inline microcopy: "Drag rungs to reorder. Click pill to configure probes and thresholds."

2) Expanded rung modal
   - Fields: name, target (model-id or variant), rollout percent, probe window (30s/1m/5m), latency SLO (ms), error SLO (%), auto-switch conditions (e.g., latency > 900ms for 2m OR error > 3% for 3 checks), cooldown period, revert-to (explicit rung id).
   - Quick toggles: enable-kv-cache-bypass, reduce-token-budget, allow-streaming-fallback.
   - Preview of expected cost delta (tokens/s + GPU-hours) vs baseline.

3) Canary composer integration
   - When saving, offer: canary to X% for Y minutes (defaults: 5% / 30m) with automatic health-checks wired to the ladder probes.
   - Canary UI should present two ladders side-by-side (control vs candidate) and a diff view for changes.

4) Emergency controls
   - Top-right red "Degrade" button maps to a fast slider: pull to degrade to next rung, hold 2s to degrade to far-right rung (max permissive).
   - Audit modal showing who triggered degrade and why (free text).

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets)
---
- RN-2101: safety-ladder SVG component + accessible keyboard support (owner: Liam)
- RN-2102: rung detail modal + validation/templating for auto-switch conditions (owner: Rosa)
- RN-2103: canary-diff view for ladder changes (owner: Ava)
- RN-2104: metrics sparkline micro-API (latency/error) for rung preview (owner: eng-observability)
- RN-2105: emergency-degrade throttle + audit trail storage (owner: SRE)
- RN-2106: cost-estimator hook for rung preview using Optimize signals (owner: product-optimize)

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
---
- Operator can create a ladder with at least 3 rungs mapping to different model variants and save as a rollout policy.
- Each rung exposes rollout percent and at least two probe thresholds (latency & error).
- Can compose a canary from ladder that auto-promotes/demotes based on probe thresholds.
- Emergency degrade control performs atomic policy switch and logs audit entry.
- UI responds to keyboard navigation and meets baseline a11y contrast.

Open questions / trade-offs
---
- Should rungs be limited to model-variant targets only, or allow region/capacity as first-class targets? (ops prefer both; UX complexity increases).
- How to represent complex boolean logic (AND/OR) for auto-switch conditions without making the modal overwhelming? Proposal: two-tier UI (simple: latency/error thresholds; advanced: rule builder).
- Persisting audit trail size — SRE wants 90-day retention, legal asks for 2 years for enterprise customers. Need cost estimate.

Edge cases and failure modes to test
---
- Partial ladder save failure: UI should rollback to last-known-good and surface a toast with reconcile diff.
- Conflicting rollouts on same route from Dedicated vs Hosted control planes — warn and show effective policy resolution.
- Flaky metrics: implement debounce for health checks to avoid oscillation (default 3 checks).

Microcopy snippets (for designers)
---
- Ladder tooltip: "Move right to allow more permissive fallbacks; move left to keep strict behavior."
- Rung status: "Healthy (0.9ms p95) — auto-promote in 6m"
- Emergency: "Degrade route: this will switch active policy immediately and may return degraded outputs."

Notes to self (informal)
---
- Prototype in Figma using actual sparkline svg and 3 color states: healthy/unstable/critical.
- Coordinate with Optimize team to fetch cost deltas for sample token distributions.
- Quick playtest with two beta customers (Fintech A, Marketplace B) — ask for feedback on permissive modes (embed-only degrade is controversial).

Next steps
---
- Designer: produce high-fidelity ladder + rung modal (due 2025-01-28).
- PM: finalize acceptance criteria and pick RN-2101..2104 for sprint 45.
- Eng: spike on SVG performance for lists of 200 routes.

End.
